Question #1
```{r}
#a.
S_Size <- c(6.5, 9.0, 8.5, 8.5, 10.5, 7.0, 9.5, 9.0, 13.0, 7.5, 10.5, 8.5, 12.0, 10.5,
13.0, 11.5, 8.5, 5.0, 10.0, 6.5, 7.5, 8.5, 10.5, 8.5, 10.5, 11.0, 9.0, 13.0)
Height <- c(66.0, 68.0, 64.5, 65.0, 70.0, 64.0, 70.0, 71.0, 72.0, 64.0, 74.5, 67.0, 71.0, 71.0,
77.0, 72.0, 59.0, 62.0, 72.0, 66.0, 64.0, 67.0, 73.0, 69.0, 72.0, 70.0, 69.0, 70.0)
Gender <- c("F", "F", "F", "F", "M", "F", "F", "F", "M", "F", "M", "F", "M", "M",
"M", "M", "F", "F", "M", "F", "F", "M", "M", "F", "M", "M", "M", "M")

shoesize <- data.frame(S_size = S_Size, Height = Height, Gender = Gender)
write.csv(shoesize, "shoesize.csv", row.names = FALSE)

#b.
shoe <-read.csv("shoesize.csv")
tail(shoe,5)

#c.
str(shoe)

#d.
dim(shoe)
nrow(shoe)
ncol(shoe)

#e.
summary(shoe)
# str() shows the structure of the data like rows and columns. 
# summary() gives statistical details like the min, mean, and median.

#f.
males   <- shoe[shoe$Gender == "M", c("S_size", "Height")]
females <- shoe[shoe$Gender == "F", c("S_size", "Height")]
males
females

#g.
mean(shoe$S_size)
mean(shoe$Height)

#h.
#Yes,taller people tend to have larger shoe sizes.


#Question 2
gender <- factor(Gender, levels = c("F", "M"), labels = c("Female", "Male"))
Gender

Question #3
```{r}
# Knitting runs from the folder where the .Rmd file is saved, making file paths relative. 
# This means the code will work for anyone as long as the CSV is kept next to the .Rmd file, 
# preventing broken computer-specific paths.```

Question #4
```{r}
str(shoe)
# Gender imports as text (chr) because read.csv() does not automatically turn text into factors. 
# If a column like S_size imports as text by mistake, mean() will return NA, sorting will be alphabetical, 
# and plots will fail, meaning you have to fix the text and convert it using as.numeric().```

Question #5
```{r}
# Checking tail() can show blank rows, typos at the bottom, or an incomplete final row. 
# You cannot spot these issues if you only look at the top using head().
```

Question #7
```{r}
mean(females$Height)
mean(males$Height)
mean(females$S_size)
mean(males$S_size)

# On average, males are taller and have larger shoe sizes than females. 
# This supports the idea that height and shoe size are linked, and shows that gender 
# should be considered when looking at this relationship.
```
